If Group A equals Group B, the odd ball must be in Group C (9-12). For the second weighing, take three balls from Group C (e.g., 9, 10, 11) and weigh them against three known good balls from Group A or B (e.g., 1, 2, 3).  
- If they balance, the odd ball is 12. A third weighing against any other ball determines if it is heavier or lighter.  
- If Group C (9-11) is heavier, one of these three is the heavier odd ball. A third weighing of 9 vs. 10 identifies the heavier one.  
- If Group C (9-11) is lighter, one of these three is the lighter odd ball. A third weighing of 9 vs. 10 identifies the lighter one.  

**Case 2: Groups A and B do not balance**  
Assume Group A is heavier than Group B (the logic applies similarly if Group B is heavier). The odd ball is either a heavier one in Group A or a lighter one in Group B. For the second weighing, weigh 1, 2, 5 (from Group A and Group B) against 3, 6, 9 (from Group A, Group B, and Group C, which are known to be normal).  
- If the left side (1, 2, 5) is heavier again, the odd ball is either 1 or 2 (heavier) or 6 (lighter). A third weighing of 1 vs. 2 determines the result.  
- If the right side (3, 6, 9) is heavier, the odd ball is either 3 (heavier) or 5 (lighter). A third weighing of 3 vs. 1 (a known good ball) identifies the odd ball.  
- If the second weighing balances, the odd ball is 4 (heavier) or 7/8 (lighter). A third weighing of 7 vs. 8 determines which is lighter.
